Contrasts for a fitted PERMANOVA

Source: R/permanova_contrasts.R
permanova_contrasts.Rd

Planned or pairwise contrasts on a fixed factor of a fitted permanova() model. Contrast families mirror emmeans. Two testing methods are offered (see method), differing in denominator and permutation scope.

Usage

permanova_contrasts(
  fit,
  type = "pairwise",
  method = c("isolated", "pooled"),
  factor = NULL,
  within = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  scores = NULL,
  custom = NULL,
  adjust = "holm",
  permutations = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

A permanova object.

type

Contrast family: "pairwise", "trt.vs.ctrl", "poly", "contr.sum", "helmert", or a contrast matrix / named list.

method

Testing method. "isolated" (default) runs each contrast as a two-group permanova() on the involved levels only - its own residual and restricted permutation; this matches PRIMER's pairwise routine and reuses the validated engine. "pooled" tests against the full-model residual with numerator SS = trace(H_c G); it borrows error df (more power) but assumes homogeneous dispersion, and its permutation null requires the engine's own generator (see Details).

factor

Name of the fixed factor. Defaults to the tested factor. Naming several factors is shorthand for the within-cell family: the first is contrasted inside combinations of the rest.

within

Optional character vector of factors whose combinations define the cells. Contrasts the levels of factor separately inside each one, rebuilding the random strata on that subset so every pair gets the denominator its own cell supports - PRIMER's "pairwise within levels" table. Dispatches to permanova_contrasts_within(); only defined for type = "pairwise".

ref

Reference level for "trt.vs.ctrl".

scores

Numeric spacing for "poly".

custom

Matrix / named list for type = "custom".

adjust

Multiplicity method for stats::p.adjust() (default "holm").

permutations

Number of permutations; defaults to fit's value.

seed

RNG seed; defaults to fit's value.

Value

An object of class permanova_contrasts, or of class permanova_contrasts_within when within is used.

Details

"isolated" is exact and fully validated: it is literally permanova() on the subset, so its statistic, denominator and permutation match a two-group analysis of those levels. "pooled" uses a numerator SS that is validated deterministically (it equals the between-group SS to machine precision), but its permutation null must be produced by the engine's Freedman-Lane generator restricted to the contrast's exchangeable units. Until that generator is wired in, "pooled" returns the statistic, df and denominator but leaves the p-value NA rather than computing it over the wrong (full-data) permutation space.

See also

permanova(), contrast_matrix(), permanova_contrasts_within()
